summary: Second full-week checkpoint on the INT8/FP8 quantization pilot. INT8 reduced cost by ~28% and added 8-12% tail latency on long prompts; FP8 showed better quality on clinical prompts but less consistent memory savings. Team agreed to expand evals, try a hybrid fallback (INT8 with FP8 for high-risk prompts), and run final live latency traces from EU. Next review set for 06/17.

Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Elliot Monroe (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Nia Rivera (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Nimbus ML Eng); Priya Shah (Nimbus Head of ML); Tom Alvarez (Nimbus Infra)

[00:00] Elliot: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and I'll hand it to Samir for the results recap.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, Priya here. Jordan and Tom on my side.
[00:22] Jordan: Jordan, yep.
[00:25] Tom: Tom.
[00:28] Elliot: Great. Samir?
[00:30] Samir: Yeah, thanks. So we ran the two quant profiles over the 7-day pilot window, INT8 and FP8. I'll start with topline numbers, then we'll dig into per-prompt quality deltas. Note there were a couple noisy runs — the EU zone had a burst of background traffic on day 4 so please ignore that for steady-state.
[01:05] Jordan: Quick clarification, when you say FP8 here, is that our custom 8-bit float kernel or vendor float8? I had a note about mixed FP8 formats.
[01:15] Samir: Good point — it's our FP8 emulation path, optimized kernel, so behavior's closer to dynamic FP8. Not vendor-specific. There may be some small variance vs pure hardware FP8.
[01:30] Priya: Ok. What were the cost numbers?
[01:34] Samir: INT8 reduced token compute cost by roughly 28% versus baseline FP16 in the hosted profile, FP8 gave about 18% savings on average but with higher variance — sometimes only 10%. Throughput improved most with INT8 in batching scenarios.
[01:55] Tom: And latency? I'm most worried about p95/p99 for our long clinical notes, we saw timeouts last week.
[02:05] Samir: Right. For short prompts (<128 tokens) both quant profiles are within 5% of FP16 median. For long prompts (~1k tokens), INT8 increased tail latency by about 8–12% at p95/p99 due to key-value cache packing overhead under INT8 kernel paths; FP8 was nearer baseline, often within 2–4%.
[02:35] Jordan: That's interesting — so INT8 gives bigger cost wins but hurts long tail latency more. Does that match your internal perf model?
